## Web API
- Today we'll study data from the [Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://www.bls.gov) (BLS).
  - [LNS14027662](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/LNS14027662)
  - [LNS14027689](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/LNS14027689)

## Dowloading data from a web API
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(blsR)
uer <- get_n_series_table(c('LNS14027662', 'LNS14027689', 'LNS14027660'), start_year = 2010, end_year = 2025)
```

## Desired plot
```{r}
#| echo: false
uer |> 
mutate(date = as.Date(paste0(as.character(year), "-", str_sub(period, 2), "-01"))) |> 
pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("L"), names_to = "series_id", values_to = "value") |>
mutate(series_id = recode(series_id,
                      LNS14027662 = "Bachelor's degree and higher",
                      LNS14027689 = "Some college",
                      LNS14027660 = "High school degree")) |>
ggplot(aes(x = date, y = value, color = series_id)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Unemployment rate by educational attainment",
       subtitle = "25 years and over, 2010-2024",
       x = "Year", y = "Unemployment rate (%)",
       color = "Educational attainment") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = make_date(2020,01,01), xmax = make_date(2022,06,01), ymin = 0, ymax = 20,
           fill = "gray", alpha = 0.3) +
  annotate("text", x = make_date(2021,03,01), y = 19, label = "COVID-19\npandemic", size = 3) +
  theme_classic()
```

## OES data
- Occupational Employment Statistics (OES) program
- Data are divided into many different tables, e.g. [May 2023](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes152051.htm)
- All the various data are available here: https://www.bls.gov/oes/tables.htm
- How to download these data and analyze them?

## Ethics of scraping data online
- You should carefully read [Section 26.2](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/webscraping.html#scraping-ethics-and-legalities) concerning various ethical and legal issues surrounding scraping data from web sites.
- In this class we will only look at large, public web sites where there is no risk of anything bad happening. 
- However, there are other situations where it may be unethical, or even illegal, to harvest data from a website, even if you are technically able. 
- **As data scientists in the real world, it will be up to you to carefully weigh these concerns before using the tools discussed in today's lecture.**

## How do web pages work?

Web pages are written in a special language called HTML (**H**yper**t**ext **M**arkup **L**anguage). Here is a simple example of some HTML:

    <html>
    <head> 
      <title>Page title</title>
    </head>
    <body>
      <h1 id='first'>A heading</h1>
      <p>Some text &amp; <b>some bold text.</b></p>
      <img src='myimg.png' width='100' height='100'>
    </body>
    
## Structure of web pages
Web scraping is possible because most web pages have a consistent, hierarchical structure. For example, if I asked you how to navigate to the title of the web page shown above, you would follow the "path"

    html > head > title
    
to arrive at "Page title".


## HTML elements

There are a lot of HTML elements that might contain interesting information. Here are a few of the most common:
  - Block tags that denote sections of text: `<h1>` (heading), `<p>` (paragraph), `<ul>`/`<ol>` (un)ordered list, etc.
  - `<table>` (a table), `<tr>` (a table row), `<td>` (a table cell), etc.
Each of these elements can contain attributes such as `id=` or `class=`. For example, `<table id="movies">` is probably a table that contains movie information.

## Inspecting a web page
To see the HTML code for a web page, right-click on the page and select "Inspect":

## <img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/The_Simpsons_yellow_logo.svg/250px-The_Simpsons_yellow_logo.svg.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="141" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/The_Simpsons_yellow_logo.svg/500px-The_Simpsons_yellow_logo.svg.png 1.5x" data-file-width="1920" data-file-height="1080">
```{webr}
#| echo: true
simpsons <- read_html("data/simpsons_1-20.html")
```

## Tables contained in page
In this page there are many tables:
```{webr}
simpsons |> html_elements("table")
```

## Extracting a specific table
We can extract a specific table by its position on the page.
```{webr}
#| echo: true
#| message: false
episodes_table <- simpsons |> html_elements("table.wikiepisodetable") |> html_table() |> list_rbind()
```

## Visualization
```{r}
#| echo: false
paste0("data/oes152051_202", 1:3, ".htm") |> 
  map(~ read_html(.x) |> html_element("table#oes15-2051_h") |> html_table()) |> 
  setNames(2021:2023) |>
  list_rbind(names_to="year") |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  mutate(annual_wage = as.integer(gsub("[$,]","",`Annual mean wage (2)`))) -> oes
ggplot(oes, aes(x=make_date(year, 1, 1), y=annual_wage / 1000, color=`State`)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(data = oes |> filter(year == 2023) |> group_by(`State`) |> slice_max(annual_wage, n=1),
            aes(label=`State`), hjust=-.1, size=3) +
  labs(title="Mean annual wage for data scientists",
       subtitle="2021-2023",
       x="Year", y="Annual mean wage (thousands of dollars)",
       color="State") +
  xlim(make_date(2021,1,1), make_date(2023,6,1)) +
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

# Quiz questions about this lecture
1. Which of the following is a legal and ethical concern when scraping data from a website?
  - A. Violating the website's terms of service
  - B. Collecting personal data without consent
  - C. Overloading the website's server with requests
  - D. All of the above
  
2. In the context of web scraping, what is HTML?
  - A. A programming language used to run a web server
  - B. A markup language used to structure web pages
  - C. A database format for storing web data
  - D. A protocol for transferring data over the internet
  
The last three questions are about the `oes` table that's loaded into your R environment.
3. For which state did mean annual wages go _down_ from 2022 to 2023?
  
4. What is the mean annual wage for data scientists in California in 2023 according to
the `oes` table?
  
5. Which state had the highest mean annual wage for data scientists in 2022 according to
the `oes` table?
